title: P02: raise five-layer Muon peak learning rate to 0.015
description: P02 follow-up: raise only peak split-QKV Muon LR from 0.01 to 0.015 on the five-layer incumbent, retaining auxiliary AdamW and the full-budget Muon schedule. Larger hidden-matrix updates may compensate for fewer updates at five layers and give fixed downstream expert iteration more transferable proof features.
hypothesis: The five-layer keep 051 increased downstream mean from 275.33 to 286.33 despite reducing updates from about 2900 to 2340. A moderate 50% increase in hidden-matrix update size may improve useful feature learning within that shorter update trajectory. This does not assume token loss diagnoses transfer: 054-codex entropy regularization degraded every downstream seed despite similar CE loss. Earlier P02 run 034 favored 0.01 over 0.02 with four layers and a 20% AdamW finish, while 035 rejected 0.005; no previous trial used 0.015 on full-budget Muon with five layers and orthogonal initialization. The new configuration tests that specific interaction rather than repeating an earlier configuration. Increased updates may instead damage proof validity or RL plasticity. MUON_WD remains defined as WD*LR/MUON_LR, changing to 0.006666666666666667 so multiplicative matrix shrinkage at each schedule fraction remains fixed. Data, architecture, initialization, schedule fraction, momentum, auxiliary optimizer and frozen RL remain unchanged. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer performance selects the candidate.
expected_delta: Central prediction +3 to +15 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 against 051-claude exact mean 286.333333 (288/260/311); plausible downside -40. Predict round-1 sample accuracy improves on at least two seeds versus 0.0630/0.0494/0.0749. Expect approximately 2300-2400 pretraining updates and similar kernel cost, with no systematic RL/eval latency increase; policy-dependent generation lengths can still change runtime. Lower pretraining loss alone cannot justify keep.

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as auxiliary AdamW; muon_lr = 0.015 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) are in Muon. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: MUON_WD=WD*LR/MUON_LR=0.006666666666666667. Muon lr*MUON_WD equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 at every schedule fraction, retaining incumbent per-step multiplicative shrinkage; total shrinkage may vary with step count.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 20 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of five blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0. No reinitialization during RL. The fifth block consumes extra global-RNG draws during construction, so random initial weights are not bitwise identical to 043's for a given seed; the init rule is identical.
